notes: Three technically plausible discovery candidates were preserved for validation: malformed-DER out-of-object pointer construction, generated-C injection through unescaped external JSON comments, and explicit trust/install of a mutable third-party Homebrew HEAD.
The lax DER signature parser uses subtraction-based bounds checks; the distinct private-key parser uses pointer-addition checks and is the preserved candidate.

Shell eval and unquoted build variables in ci/ci.sh are fed by repository-controlled workflow configuration, and the run-in-docker command input has only static in-repository callers; no hostile source-to-sink path was preserved.
Examples print freshly generated demonstration values and may exit without full cleanup on failure, but no production secret asset or realistic hostile boundary was identified.

All assigned text files were reviewed from start to finish. No binary or generated item was unreviewable, and supporting workflow call sites were inspected only where needed to complete candidate paths.
